..
An impending trough extending from Invest 97W to the east will move
westward through the region, bringing gusty winds, increased shower 
coverage, and thunderstorm potential over the weekend, potentially 
peaking on Sunday. As 97W moves into the Philippine Sea, a monsoon 
pattern will trail behind, enveloping the Marianas possibly for the 
entirety of next week. Because the timing of this pattern is more 
than three days out, shower coverage was kept at scattered, however, 
increasing into the late week to convey the possibility of the 
monsoon strengthening. Winds will become moderate starting tomorrow, 
with stronger gusts near heavier showers on Sunday before.

Marine...
The westerly swell from distant Typhoon Bavi (09W) continues to keep
combined seas and surf hazardous, so the Small Craft Advisory, High 
Surf Advisory, and High Risk of Rip Currents along north, south, and
west facing reefs were extended to early Saturday morning. A
secondary easterly swell will reach the Marianas, potentially
increasing in height by a foot or two throughout the week, but will
most likely remain below hazardous conditions along east facing 
reefs. Unsettled weather will bring moderate winds with gusts near
heavier showers, scattered showers, and isolated thunderstorms over 
the weekend.

Tropical Systems...
Invest 97W is located near 5.2N 154.2E, just southeast of Chuuk. The
Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC) continues 97W as sub-low, 
meaning tropical cyclone development is not expected for the next few
days. Invest 97W is expected to continue moving west to west-
northwest remaining largely disorganized, before lifting northwest 
into the Philippine Sea and away from the region. Currently, 
scattered to numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms are 
associated mainly across the western half of this feature, which will
bring unsettled weather to Chuuk over the weekend.

Eastern Micronesia...
The main weather story will be a wet and active stretch is taking
shape for the next 10 days, possibly longer. This is due to the re-
emergence of the NET (Near-Equatorial Trough), which stretches east
from Invest 97W (south of Pohnpei), to another broad/weak circulation
southeast of Majuro near 4N178E. The NET continues east past the Date
Line. Looking upstream east of there, several troughs are embedded 
in the easterly flow, stretching as far east as 155W (south of 
Hawaii). Additionally, the MJO will return to the area at the end of 
the month. Typically, we see an increase in convective activity as it
begins to "nudge" into the Western Micronesia and the FSM. 
Extrapolating between the two...it all points to a fairly active 
period potentially taking hold for a while. With this in mind, we 
increased rainfall potential through much of the forecast, with most 
areas seeing at least scattered showers through the forecast period.

As for marine conditions, light to gentle winds will occasionally
become gentle to moderate area-wide through the forecast, with seas
of 4 to 6 feet anticipated.

Western Micronesia...
The High Surf Advisory and Small Craft Advisory has been extended 
through Saturday afternoon for Yap, and, these advisories has been 
allowed to expire for Palau. 

For Palau, seas and surf have fallen below the critical thresholds 
of 10 foot seas and 9 foot surf, however, seas and surf remain just 
below these heights. Seas may fluctuate around these cricial levels.
Showers are expected to start building in tonight and anticipated to
remain in the area for much of the forecast period. To start the 
forecast period off these showers are expected to be monsoonal in 
nature. These showers are expected to transition to showers produced
by Invest 97W once it moves closer to Palau. Overall, periods of 
low- to high-end scattered showers are anticipated through the 
middle of next week.

For Yap, the seas and surf are remaining just above the 10 foot seas
and 9 foot surf thresholds, so the Small Craft Advisory and High Surf
Advisory along west and north reefs were extended for another day. 
Seas and surf are expected to drop below thresholds as early as 
Saturday afternoon. Like Palau, showers are expected through the 
middle of next week, however, are anticipated to be a bit more 
intense compared to Palau. Showers here are expected to range from 
scattered to widespread with the peak shower potential being Saturday
night through Sunday night, showers during this time period may be 
heavy at times. 

For Chuuk, satellite imagery shows a lot of cells of showers in the
nearby oceanic waters. Showers are expected to build back in for the
weekend and beginning part of next week as Invest 97W passes to the 
south of the lagoon. These showers may be heavy at times, however at 
this time there is no flooding concerns. Showers may break as early 
as Tuesday once 97W move out of Chuuk's region. Overall a wet weekend
and beginning of next week, will taper down to a trade-wind pattern 
by mid week.
